svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A section through human skin."], [1, "Three layers: epidermis, dermis and subcutaneous fat."], [4, "Too hot: sweat glands secrete sweat, which evaporates and cools the skin."], [6.5, "Too hot: arterioles dilate, so more blood flows near the surface and loses heat by radiation."], [10, "Too cold: erector muscles contract and raise the hairs; arterioles constrict."]]
svg.title: The structure of skin
svg.desc: A section through skin: epidermis, dermis and subcutaneous fat, with a hair and follicle, erector muscle, sebaceous gland, sweat gland and duct, blood vessels and sensory receptors; animated responses to heat and cold.
svg.text: Section, simplified and not to scale.

g.data-info: Adipose tissue: insulation, energy store and cushioning.
Thick layer of connective tissue with blood vessels, nerves, sweat glands, hair follicles and sensory receptors.
Outer layer of stratified epithelium. The surface cells are dead and full of keratin: a waterproof barrier against pathogens. Melanin protects against UV.
Arterioles to the surface capillaries dilate when hot (more heat lost) and constrict when cold.
Hairs grow from follicles. The erector muscle raises the hair to trap a layer of air.
Secretes sebum, an oily substance that keeps hair and skin supple and is antimicrobial.
Secretes sweat; evaporation of sweat from the skin surface takes heat from the body.
Detect touch, pressure, pain and temperature; send impulses along sensory neurones.
